## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix mixed-case writes before merge because the new `Cache.set` method can store entries that `Cache.get` cannot retrieve. Entries also remain readable at their expiration deadline.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, the default TTL constant, and expiration.

## Critical

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("ALPHA", 1)`, `get("ALPHA")` returns `None` on a fresh cache. `set` stores the original key, while `get` looks up `key.lower()`. — Callers that write mixed-case keys get cache misses even when they read back using the same spelling.

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — When `set("alpha", 1)` writes at monotonic time `1000` with `ttl=1`, it stores a deadline of `1001`, but `get("alpha")` still returns `1` at `1001` because `app/cache.py:21` uses a strict less-than comparison. — A caller reading at the configured expiration instant can receive a value whose lifetime has ended. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` in `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire`.

## Suggestions

- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test the default cache lifetime through reads — For an entry written with `Cache()`, the test still passes if the entry expires after 60 seconds while `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` remains `300`. The assertion checks the constant without exercising expiration. — A regression that disconnects default entry expiration from the configured constant would pass this test. — Fix: Use a controlled clock in `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to exercise reads on both sides of the five-minute deadline.
